title: Priority slate reservation for strategic accounts (mini-roadmaps and commitment windows)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Build a deterministic "priority slate" feature that reserves discrete roadmap capacity (mini-roadmaps) and timeboxed commitment windows for strategic/top accounts. The slate formalizes commitments: number of sprints, scope bucket, and fallbacks. Background: Enterprise accounts repeatedly request accelerated delivery and escalations which collide with our PLG pipeline and existing prioritization heuristics. We need a predictable protocol to accept a bounded set of top-account asks into a sprint runway while protecting platform velocity and SLA guarantees. Objectives: 1) Create an intake form + scoring model tuned for strategic accounts; 2) Define capacity reservation units (SRUs) that map to sprint points and calendar windows; 3) Expose a dashboard for committed vs. available slate capacity; 4) Automate acceptance/decline triggers with recommended fallbacks and handoffs to Solutions/CS. Constraints: limited engineering capacity, cross-team dependencies (infra, console, legal for contractual obligations), and public roadmap transparency trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Intake form version v1 implemented and integrated into customer success intake flow (fields: impact, ARR attribution, legal constraints, security needs, opt-in for private deployments)
AC2: Scoring model produces a deterministic numeric score and recommendation (fast-track / needs review / decline) and is documented in the PRD
AC3: Slate capacity units (SRUs) defined with conversion to story points and calendar windows; product + eng agree on conversion table
AC4: UI: Console shows slate dashboard with committed SRUs, pending requests, and countdown to window close

AC5: Automation: When a request is accepted, Linear ticket is created with prefilled scope template and a 'commitment' label; customers receive standardized commitment email with SLA and fallback policy
AC6: Telemetry: Metric endpoints available in Datadog/Grafana for "committed_sru_usage", "accepted_requests_by_account", and "overcommit_events"
AC7: Legal/Finance sign-off flow mocked in Confluence and tested for one pilot account
proposed_solution: Implement a three-part system: (1) intake + scoring microservice (serverless) that consumes CS/AM inputs and computes a priority score; (2) reservation engine in the roadmap service that mints SRUs and holds capacity for a timeboxed window; (3) Console feature to visualize and manage slates. The scoring model will weight account MRR, strategic signal (partnership/marketing), churn risk, escalation severity, and technical feasibility. Fallbacks: per-request fallback plan that lists compatible model variants or deferred windows.
metrics: Time to intake decision (target < 5 business days)
% of top-account requests converted to committed SRU (target 30% initial pilot)
Committed SRU utilization vs forecast (target within ±10%)
Number of overcommit incidents per quarter (target 0 during pilot)
Customer satisfaction (CSAT) for committed deliveries (target > 4/5 for pilot accounts)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Week 1-2): Finalize PRD + scoring rubric; stakeholder alignment with Sales, CS, Legal
Phase 1 (Week 3-6): Build intake form and scoring microservice; create SRU conversion table with Eng leads
Phase 2 (Week 7-9): Implement reservation engine and Console dashboard mock; run tabletop with 2 pilot accounts
Phase 3 (Week 10-12): Pilot with 3 strategic customers; collect telemetry and refine thresholds
Phase 4 (Week 13): Decision gate: expand to GA or revisit policy parameters based on pilot results
